chapter: The 1940s: small groups, Teddy Wilson and Ethel Waters
title: Chile's Restaurant and the standing ovation after surgery
summary: Babe dates this to 1945-46. Thomas left the hospital under Dr. Arthur Logan for his Sunday gig at Chile's, and the crowd gave him a long standing ovation as he walked to the men's room.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What year was this? Do you remember, Babe?

This had to be I'd say around '42, '43 because so many things went together because within that time, if I'm not mistaken, this came up and then Grossingers. Grossings was '45. And then right behind that we did some more college dates and then Joe went back to try to form his own little group again. And then Chiles came in there.
Chiles?
Chiles Restaurant.
Who were you in there with?
My group.
With his own group. And he did a tremendous thing. He took sick and I had to put him in the hospital for a minor operation.
I remember that. You and the doctor put me in the hospital.

Doctor Arthur Logan and he had this date at Chiles so they weren't going to release him until say like the following Monday or Tuesday but this date for Sunday afternoon was already booked and he talked to the doctors and the doctor that operated on
JT (1 of 2)
him and his doctor, which was Dr. Arthur Logan, and mainly to Dr. Logan.
Beautiful doctor.

And he really understood, and still does, musicians are performers and he told Dr. Logan, I've got to get out of at here because I've got to do this date in Chiles. So, Dr. Logan blow said, You can't ge. You were just operated on. But he said, But, I've got to. So to make a long story short, Dr. Logan had him released. Told him to be very careful, released him on a Saturday evening, that Sunday afternoon, Joe had to work. Well, I wasn't working with him that Sunday afternoon but, naturally I went with him because, naturally, I was very con- cerned and I saw one of the most beautiful things happen. quite a few I've seen/beautiful things happen to Joe in the times since we have been married, career-wise, but this was one of the most beautiful things I've ever seen. When the group he had with him that particular day finished, when they finished a session, Joe fought through it and when he finished, he had to go, I know it's on tape and all that, but he had to go to the bathroom. And, in turn, he couldn't walk fast. He had to walk very, very slow and he finishes up and he gets off the bandstand and he starts toward the bathroom. Well, it was like a standing They wanted him back ovation. It-was,-in-fact to play an other number or so and the people are watching him. The place was packed. They're watching
JT (1 of 2)

him walk away from the bandstand and they're applauding and so then they stand up and they keep applauding. And, I've got my eyes on him and I'm watching him and it takes him, Stanley, no kidding, at least 5 minutes to walk to the men's room and the people are still applauding.
That place was (...?)
It really was.
... Fairmont Theater.
He goes to the bathroom
It-also-was-the- comes out and he starts back so he can sit down and the house is tremendous. It won't stop. It's a standing ovation. People are just screaming and applauding.
I didn't know what they were applauding for.
He don't even know what's happening. He goes to get back to the bandstand but he don't get on the bandstand, the fellows are off and the people are just continuing to applaud.
Did they know you'd been ...
Oh, no.
... (too many talking at once)

But, at this time he can't do anything with the people the MC can't /so he gets back on the bandstand and this is when he announces that Joe Thomas had just been released from the hospital the day before from a minor operation and he appreciates everything that they're doing and how the people have received him but he can't come back on the stand. And that house refused to stop. It was like a 15 minute standing ovation.
He must have played mighty good.
JT (1 of 2)

He did. He really did and he had to get back on that stand. He played one short number but I'll never get for/it because I sat there and I said, Oh my goodness, what in the world is he going to do. But, it was absolutely ...
What do you mean, I said what.
